annotation.authors_or_issuer: Khan, O.; Alberta, M.; Lee, D.
key_provisions_or_claims: Proposes moral conditioning ('bumper theory') so robots become morally responsible agents, addressing the responsibility gap.
Implements Haidt's Moral Foundations Theory as a social-learning rulebook for robots.
Uses computer vision (YOLO, MTCNN) on Jetson Nano to detect humans, dogs and cars to avoid collisions.
Finds YOLOv4-tiny best suited to the constrained Jetson Nano environment.
Asimov's Three Laws are deemed insufficient for autonomous vehicles.
annotation.summary_en: Research article addressing the robot responsibility gap by proposing moral conditioning ('bumper theory') based on Moral Foundations Theory. It tests YOLO and MTCNN vision models on a Jetson Nano to detect humans and vehicles for collision avoidance, concluding YOLOv4-tiny is best suited for making robots responsible moral agents.
annotation.title_clean: Responsible Robots and AI Via Moral Conditioning
annotation.title_en: Responsible Robots and AI Via Moral Conditioning
annotation.venue: Online Journal of Robotics & Automation Technology
